extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Spectator; educated general readers, writers, critics, and polite society seeking literary and social advice
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and critical criteria for the sentiments and use of humour in epic (heroic) poetry, with related prescriptive advice on agreeable behaviour and methods for personal advancement that the essays present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnatural or affected sentiments in epic poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: An Epic Poet should not only avoid such Sentiments as are unnatural or affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sentiments must feel proper to the poem's dignity and seriousness; affected or artificial thoughts undermine the heroic tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mean and vulgar sentiments in epic poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: An Epic Poet should avoid such Sentiments as are mean and vulgar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low, groveling, or vulgar notions are inappropriate to epic scale; even if such thoughts may be natural in some contexts, they degrade the magnificence essential to the heroic poem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit laughter-inducing sentiments in epic; preserve serious air
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentiments which raise Laughter can very seldom be admitted with any Decency into an Heroic Poem, whose Business it is to excite Passions of a much nobler Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Epic poetry's chief aim is to move noble passions; humour should be used sparingly and only where it does not break the poem's dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow humour only when well-timed and contextually appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Small pieces of mirth are permissible when well timed and placed in an appropriate book/section (e.g., the 'Book of Games and Diversions').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the laugh at Monætes in the fifth book of the Aeneid is excused because it occurs in a relaxed, diversionary section where the reader's mind may be prepared for entertainment; placement and timing determine acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid puns and weak pleasantries in epic
rubrics_metrics.description: Puns and low pleasantries (a 'String of Punns') are exceptionable in epic poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such devices diminish the poem's grandeur; Milton's passage of devils' puns is singled out as particularly objectionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context can excuse homeliness in ancient epics
rubrics_metrics.description: Apparent homeliness in Homer is attributed to the simplicity of his age and of that which he described, not necessarily an imperfection in the poet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should consider historical and cultural context before condemning homely or coarse images as faults in ancient epic poets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burlesque characterization risks departing from epic seriousness
rubrics_metrics.description: When characters or scenes lapse into the burlesque, the poem departs from the serious air essential to epic magnificence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homer's portrayals of Vulcan, Thersites, Irus, and the Mars-Venus story are examples where burlesque elements approach impropriety for epic; such treatment should be used cautiously and sparingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain dignity by matching sentiment to subject and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: A poem's sentiments should align with the subject's gravity and the poem's magnificent tone; incongruous levity or groveling sentiment disrupts unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a given sentiment serves the poem's aim to excite noble passions; reject those that produce only laughter or triviality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasing others should flow from benevolence, not vanity
rubrics_metrics.description: If your concern for pleasing others arises from innate benevolence, it succeeds; if from vanity to excel, its disappointment is certain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motive matters: genuine desire to please (benevolence) creates agreeable behaviour, while affectation and vanity produce the fop or parasite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreeableness depends on natural disposition, not affectation
rubrics_metrics.description: An agreeable man is endowed with the natural bent to do acceptable things from delight in them; the affectation of that character constitutes a fop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate sincerity and naturalness rather than contrivance; affectation is recognized and disliked by discerning company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delicacy of sentiment and chastity of thought foster select conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: A rational and select conversation is composed of persons who have the talent of pleasing with delicacy of sentiments flowing from habitual chastity of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid constrained, obscene, and painful witticisms; refined conversation depends on purity and delicacy of ideas, not forced humour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity is essential to pleasing and commands approbation
rubrics_metrics.description: The happy talent of pleasing seems wholly owing to the opinion others have of your sincerity; sincerity forces the approbation even of opponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrable candour and affability make a person agreeable even when they possess power; cultivate genuine behaviour rather than flattery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid importunity and speaking immodestly of one's wants to patrons
rubrics_metrics.description: One should avoid taking all opportunities to speak of one's own wants; this shamelessness repels rather than moves compassion in patrons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When soliciting favour, make requests modest and appear not troublesome; the main art is to be as little troublesome as possible and make hopes come as favours rather than claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not prostitute yourself by adapting entirely to a patron's humour
rubrics_metrics.description: Falling in with the particular humour or manner of one above you, abstracted from general rules of good behaviour, is the life of a slave; a parasite gives up his soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain integrity and independent character rather than subservient imitation; being useful or agreeable is acceptable, but self-abasement is dishonourable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wealth eases social success but is not a true substitute for character
rubrics_metrics.description: Be rich (satirical maxim): acknowledged merit and fortune add weight and dignity to behaviour and make agreeable conduct easier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While wealth can make indifferent actions appear graceful and secure patronage, it is a pragmatic shortcut rather than a moral recommendation; cultivate virtues too.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thrift (saving) as a primary method to grow rich
rubrics_metrics.description: The first and most infallible method toward attaining wealth is thrift; saving small sums accumulates a competent fortune.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical frugality and avoiding unnecessary small expenditures are widely available means to accumulate wealth over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence as essential to acquiring fortune
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligence justly claims the next place to thrift as a means of growing rich.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent industry and application are key; industrious people can gain fortunes even without superior natural talents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method in business: focus and single-tasking
rubrics_metrics.description: Method in business is crucial: do one thing at once and give complete attention until tasks are finished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orderly disposition of affairs often leads to success where brilliant but scattered minds fail; prioritize and finish before moving on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventiveness and commerce offer additional routes to wealth
rubrics_metrics.description: There is room for genius — invention, new trades, and commerce can create fortunes where thrift and diligence alone may not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrepreneurial novelty (finding new products, cheaper materials, imaginative schemes) and trade are natural and often effective ways to acquire wealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thrift may not suit high ambition focused on large designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Saving is not designed for men pushing themselves to the top of states or forming great designs; thrift can disappoint ambitious ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the limits of thrift: those pursuing great political or artistic ambition may need to prioritize resources differently and focus on large-scale projects.
